---
title: 'flora_distribution_gap'
description: 'Find candidate new Brazilian state records for a plant or algal taxon'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---


```{r}
#| eval: false
floraR::flora_distribution_gap()
```

### Description

Given a genus or species of plants or algae, checks [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org)
and, optionally, the [Reflora
Virtual Herbarium](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/herbarioVirtual/) and [speciesLink](https://specieslink.net) for specimen and
occurrence evidence of the taxon in Brazilian states that are *not* currently
listed in its official Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) distribution. This flags
candidate new state records for a taxonomist to verify - e.g. a species listed by FFB
only for Bahia, but with herbarium specimens from Pernambuco - so that the
distributions in FFB monographs can be kept complete. Georeferenced records are also
placed in the six Brazilian phytogeographic domains, to flag candidate new domain
records in the same way.

### Details

**FFB side.** The officially listed states come from the parsed FFB taxon and
distribution tables (the same locally cached dataset as `flora_records`).
For a genus, the states of all its species and infraspecific taxa are combined; for a
species, those of the species and its infraspecific taxa. If the name is a synonym in
FFB, the distribution of its accepted name is used.

**Occurrence evidence.** Up to three sources can be queried (see
`sources`):

- `"gbif"` (default): GBIF's public API, which aggregates most Brazilian herbaria. The name is first resolved to its GBIF backbone key among plants and algae only (so, e.g., the red alga *Gracilaria* is not confused with the moth genus of the same name), so the records of its synonyms and infraspecific taxa are included. All states are counted in a single request.
- `"reflora"`: REFLORA herbarium specimens, via `reflora_records` (requires the refloraR package). Note that the first use downloads the Reflora herbarium archives - several gigabytes - which refloraR then caches for later calls.
- `"speciesLink"`: speciesLink's API, which requires a free API key (`specieslink_key`; create one at https://specieslink.net).

Free-text state values in these sources (e.g. `"Ba"`, `"Est. do Bahia"`,
`"Paraiba"`) are normalised to FFB state names before comparison; values that are
not Brazilian states are ignored.

**Phytogeographic domains.** With `domains = TRUE` (default), the GBIF
records that have coordinates - excluding those GBIF flags with geospatial issues,
such as zero coordinates or coordinates outside the stated country - are placed in
the six Brazilian phytogeographic domains (Amazonia, Caatinga, Cerrado, Mata
Atlantica, Pampa, Pantanal) using IBGE's biome map (2019) bundled with floraR,
simplified to a 1 km tolerance. A domain with records but not listed for the taxon
in FFB is a candidate new domain record. Up to `max_coordinates` records are
read (300 per request); REFLORA specimens with coordinates are added when
`"reflora"` is among `sources`. Records that fall outside the six domains
(e.g. just offshore) are kept in `records`, with `Domain = NA`, but
are never flagged nor drawn on the report's map. This
analysis requires the sf package, and the map in the HTML report the
leaflet package; without them, they are skipped with a message.

Occurrence records are evidence to review, not proof: a record in a new state may be
a cultivated plant, a misidentification, or a georeferencing error, which is why the
HTML report lists the individual records behind each candidate state.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| taxon | Character. A single genus or species name of plants or algae (e.g. `"Luetzelburgia auriculata"` or `"Luetzelburgia"`). |
| state | Character vector. Optional subset of Brazilian states (full name or acronym) to restrict the check to. `NULL` (default) checks all states with any evidence. |
| sources | Character vector. Which occurrence sources to query: any of `"gbif"`, `"reflora"`, `"speciesLink"`. Defaults to `"gbif"`, the fastest. See Details for the requirements of the other two. |
| specieslink_key | Character. speciesLink API key, used when `"speciesLink"` is among `sources`. Defaults to the `SPECIESLINK_KEY` environment variable. |
| domains | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), also place the georeferenced records in the Brazilian phytogeographic domains and flag candidate new domain records (see Details). Requires the sf package. |
| max_coordinates | Numeric. Maximum number of georeferenced GBIF records read for the domain analysis. Defaults to `5000`. |
| version | Character. FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to `"latest"`. Passed to `flora_download`. |
| verbose | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |
| save | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), the result is saved to disk as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet. |
| dir | Character. Directory where the spreadsheet is saved when `save = TRUE`. Defaults to `"flora_distribution_gap"`. |
| filename | Character. Name of the `.xlsx` file (without extension) to save. Defaults to `"flora_distribution_gap_<taxon>"`. |
| html_report | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), also writes a self-contained HTML report (`<dir>/<filename>.html`) summarizing the results: KPI counts, an evidence-by-source breakdown, the full state-by-state table, the domain table, an interactive map of the georeferenced records over the phytogeographic domains (coloured by candidate status), the records in candidate domains, and the individual occurrence records found in the new-state-record candidate states - each linking to the record in its source database - all as sortable, filterable DT widgets with buttons to copy or download them as CSV/Excel. Requires the rmarkdown, DT, and htmltools packages; if any is missing, the report is skipped with a message (the `.xlsx` spreadsheet is unaffected). |
| open_report | Logical. If `TRUE` (default in interactive sessions), opens the HTML report in the browser once rendered. |

### Value

A list of three `data.frame`s:

- `states`: One row per Brazilian state with any evidence for `taxon` (in FFB or in the queried sources): `Taxon`, `State`, `In_FFB_distribution` (whether FFB already lists the state), `GBIF_records`, `Reflora_records`, and `speciesLink_records` (records in the state, for each source queried), and `New_state_record_candidate` (`TRUE` when the state has evidence from at least one source but is not in FFB's distribution).
- `domains`: One row per phytogeographic domain with evidence (in FFB or among the georeferenced records): `Taxon`, `Domain`, `In_FFB_distribution`, `Georeferenced_records`, and `New_domain_record_candidate`. Empty when `domains = FALSE`.
- `records`: One row per georeferenced record, with its coordinates, `State`, `Domain`, collector, date, institution, catalogue number, identification, a link to the record, and the logical columns `New_state_record_candidate` and `New_domain_record_candidate`. Empty when `domains = FALSE`.

With `save = TRUE`, each table is saved as a sheet of the `.xlsx`
spreadsheet.

### Examples

```r
# Candidate new state records for a species
gap <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata")

# A whole genus, restricted to two states
gap_ne <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia",
                                 state = c("Pernambuco", "Paraiba"))

# The candidate new phytogeographic domains, and the records behind them
gap$domains
gap$records[gap$records$New_domain_record_candidate, ]

# Adding REFLORA herbarium specimens (requires refloraR)
gap_reflora <- flora_distribution_gap(taxon = "Luetzelburgia auriculata",
                                      sources = c("gbif", "reflora"))
```
